newsitem.title: LATVIA: ROJA SEES 1997 TURNOVER DOWN, TO BOOST CAPACITY.
newsitem.headline: ROJA SEES 1997 TURNOVER DOWN, TO BOOST CAPACITY.

text.p: Fish cannery Roja, quoted on the stock market's secondary list, on Wednesday said that it expected 1997 turnover to be lower but it would boost capacity.
"Our turnover will be reduced in 1997," Igor Nikitin, the company's export manager, told Reuters.
The company would not release any 1996 results yet as the audit procedure of the previous year's balance sheet had only started today.
"We are seeing more competition, especially from Estonian producers and the price of our tinned fish has already been pressed down to 40 santimes from 45," he said.
All Roja's produce is currently exported, with the main markets being Ukraine, Kazakhstan and Israel.
"This year the share of our exports to Russia is going down but Germany, the U.S. and Canada seem promising," he adeded.
Company deputy board chairman Valdis Simpsons said Roja plans to double its production capacity as a new tinned fish production facility comes into full operation in April or May.
"We will double our capacity of producing tinned fish from 700,000 a month on average in 1996 when the new facility comes into operation," he told Reuters.
"We will produce mainly tinned sprats there but the volume will totally depend on the demand," he added.
The facility is expected to create some 100 new jobs in the factory, which at the moment employs 565 people.
Simpsons said Roja was investing in both its fleet, production and harbour facilities.
"We are investing heavily," Simpsons said. "We are leasing three ships with an option to buy them and have started getting our quay in an orderly shape."
